welcome.title: CLLG — Guided Tour
welcome.body: CLLG turns scans of Greek and Latin scholarship into structured TEI XML in six steps: import, mask, OCR, structure, review and export. Recognition runs locally with Kraken. The demo project is the start of the editio princeps of Galen's De propriis placitis (V. Boudon-Millot & A. Pietrobelli, Revue des Études Grecques 118, 2005), distributed by Persée under a CC BY-NC-ND licence. It is full of small challenges; nothing you do in the tour is saved.

home-new-project.title: Step 1 · Import your document
home-new-project.body: Click «New project» to load a PDF or DjVu, then choose the pages to import: a range such as «2-40», or quick filters like «Skip covers». Each page becomes an image in a project folder on your machine. In the demo, page 1 is the Persée cover: it is skipped for OCR but kept in the project, because it records where the document comes from and under which licence.

home-sources.title: Other sources
home-sources.body: You can also start from a folder of page images, or from ALTO XML files with their images (e.g. exported from eScriptorium). ALTO import keeps each line's geometry; if the ALTO carries LADaS zone types, paragraphs, quotes and headings are detected automatically.

masker-canvas.title: Step 2 · Mask what shouldn't be read
masker-canvas.body: Draw white rectangles over everything that is not the main text: masked areas are whited out before Kraken reads the page. Page 2 of the demo has three: the running head («172  V. BOUDON-MILLOT ET A. PIETROBELLI»), the line numbers in the left margin (5, 10, 15…) and the footnotes. Challenge: page 3 prints its line numbers in the right margin — does it need a mask too?

masker-tools.title: Masking tools
masker-tools.body: Rectangle mask (D) draws, Pointer (S) selects, Delete removes. «Copy to all pages» repeats a layout across the book; hover a thumbnail and click ⊘ to skip a page (like the cover). «Generate masks from ALTO regions» builds masks from imported zones and «Export COCO» saves them as training data.

ocr-models.title: Step 3 · Choose the Kraken models
ocr-models.body: Kraken uses a segmentation model (finds the lines) and a recognition model (reads them). The built-in Ancient Greek models work out of the box; choose Custom to load your own. «CPU threads» sets how much of the computer OCR may use — saved for this computer.

ocr-run.title: Run OCR
ocr-run.body: Click «Run OCR» to recognize the queued pages one at a time; results are cached, so you can stop and resume at any time. Each line is anchored with <lb n="…"/> so the text stays linked to its place on the image. Below: Kraken's raw output for the start of page 2 — a lowercase ν in the title, a stray υ, a lost «(ἐν)» and a missing iota subscript.

config-hierarchy.title: Step 4 · Define the document structure
config-hierarchy.body: Describe how the text is divided and numbered. This treatise is divided into sections 1, 2, 3…, so the demo has a single level, «section», with Arabic numbers. The hierarchy drives the TEI <div> structure; the Bibliography section fills the TEI header's sourceDesc (the demo already cites the article).

config-format.title: Reference patterns
config-format.body: Choose the numbering system of each level: Roman (I II III), Arabic (1 2 3), Greek (α β γ), or a custom regex. Options: missing_first (the first number is not printed), allow_gaps, and milestone (a marker inside the text, such as a page reference, rather than a division).

review-editor.title: Step 5 · Review and correct
review-editor.body: The scan is on the left, the transcription on the right; the button at the left of the page bar hides the scan. Edit directly and save with ⌘S (⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z undo and redo); change page with the arrows at the top right or Ctrl+↑ / Ctrl+↓. Below: the same lines as the OCR step, after review. Challenge: page 3 still hides two OCR slips — find «ομὲν» and «τῆν».

review-image.title: Line boxes and zones
review-image.body: «Show line boxes» outlines every line; click one to jump to it in the editor. «Draw Zone» (G, pointer over the image) groups lines: press P, Q, H or C for Paragraph, Quote, Heading or Continued, then draw; click a zone to move or resize it, Delete removes it. In the demo, page 2's title is a Heading, and page 3 opens with a Continued zone: section 2 carries on from page 2, and the export joins them. To fix a badly segmented line, select it, press R over the image and draw its new box; «Re-OCR line» reads that line again.

review-tag-ref.title: Tag the section numbers
review-tag-ref.body: Select a section number and press ⌘R to wrap it in <ref>; the tag dock at the bottom assigns its level (here, 1 = section). Each level-1 <ref> opens a new <div> at export. Also: ⌘M <note>, ⌘Q <quote>, ⌘I <cit>, ⌘B <bibl>.

review-tools.title: Checking tools and Greek typing
review-tools.body: «2nd read» runs Kraken again and underlines disagreements; «Line» shows the image of the current line above the caret; the magnifier (⌘F) searches the page; «Latin» flags Latin letters inside Greek. β (⌘K) is a betacode keyboard, diacritics first: «)a» gives ἀ, «:» the ano teleia ·, «?» the Greek question mark, and «<» «>» the Leiden brackets ⟨ ⟩ that this edition uses for supplied words (page 2: «περὶ ⟨ὧν⟩»).

export-generate.title: Step 6 · Export
export-generate.body:
«Generate» builds one TEI P5 file for the whole document: each section opens a

, and a Continued zone is merged into the paragraph it continues — across the — as in the real output below. Words split at the line end, like «διά-» / «νοιαν», are joined with . The Per-page tab exports plain text, LADaS-tagged text, ALTO or pre-TEI; you can also export a searchable PDF or share the project as a zip.

finale.title: You're ready!
finale.body: Import a PDF, a folder of images or ALTO files and start your own edition; the tour can be replayed from the home screen or the sidebar. Help improve the models: sharing your original data — page images with their corrected transcriptions (ALTO or per-page exports; the final TEI is not required) — with the CLLG developers helps train better segmentation and recognition. The demo pages come from Persée (doi:10.3406/reg.2005.4610) under CC BY-NC-ND.
